intro: Bandwar is a historic village in the Begusarai district of Bihar, located about 18 km from the district headquarters. Whether you are an NRI returning to your roots, a researcher, or a traveler, here is a comprehensive guide on how to reach Bandwar using air, rail, and road networks.

options.details: The nearest airport is Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport (PAT) in Patna, which is approximately 125 km away. From Patna, you can hire a taxi (takes about 2 to 2.5 hours) or take a train to Begusarai. Another option is Darbhanga Airport (DBR), which is also well-connected to major Indian cities. From either airport, the onward journey to Begusarai is by road or rail.

The nearest railway station is Begusarai Railway Station (BGS), located about 15-18 km from Bandwar. It has three platforms and is well-connected to major cities like Patna, Delhi, Kolkata, and Guwahati. Major trains like the Koshi Express, Intercity Express, and Rajya Rani Express connect Patna to Begusarai. The nearby Barauni Junction is a major rail hub in the region. From the station, you can hire an auto or taxi to reach the village.

Bandwar is well-connected via National Highway 31 (NH-31) and State Highway 55 (SH-55). Patna is about 124 km away and can be reached by bus or car. Regular buses and shared jeeps run frequently from Patna and other major cities. From the Begusarai bus stand, you can easily get a shared auto or e-rickshaw to Bandwar. Private buses also operate directly to the village.

Once you reach Bandwar, e-rickshaws and auto-rickshaws are the primary means of local transport. The main landmarks to identify the village entrance are the Shaheed Ramchandra Dwar (Main Gate) and the SBI Bank branch. Fares are nominal; it is advisable to agree on the fare before starting your journey.

Bandwar does not have commercial hotels or guest houses. Visitors typically stay with relatives or commute from Begusarai town. Begusarai has several decent options for accommodation, including Hotel Kamala Inn, Hotel Royal, Zero Mile Rooms, Kasa Courtyard & Banquets, and Hotel Harsh Garden. It is highly recommended to book your stay in Begusarai in advance.

The best time to visit Bandwar is during the winter months (November to February) when the weather is pleasant and comfortable for travel. Summers (March to June) can be extremely hot. The monsoon season (July to September) brings heavy rainfall and can cause flooding in the region, which might disrupt travel plans.

While in Bandwar, you can also explore the nearby Kanwar (Kabartal) Lake Bird Sanctuary, a Ramsar-listed wetland and one of Asia's largest oxbow lakes, located about 22 km from Begusarai town. The Naulakha Temple in Garhpura and the Simaria Ghat on the Ganges are also notable local heritage and pilgrimage sites.
